exposure: indication for cesarean section (uterine rupture, hemorrhage)
cohort: The study included records of 37,585 cesarean sections performed at 14 regional referral hospitals and 14 first-level (district) hospitals in Uganda.
finding: Uterine rupture, hemorrhage, emergency surgery, and general anesthesia were identified as predictors of worse immediate neonatal outcomes, including higher rates of low Apgar scores, neonatal mortality, and stillbirths.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections and the use of general anesthesia were associated with worse neonatal outcomes compared to elective surgery and spinal anesthesia, respectively.
followup_time: Immediate (Apgar score at 1 and 5 minutes; immediate neonatal death, stillbirth)
